clarification_sequence_scenario.description: Integration check for multi-attempt clarification and fallback sequence (reserved for F6/F7, not an additional test case)

steps.description: Submit T07 for q1 with no prior unclear attempt. Expect clarification and no diagnosis.
Submit T11 utterance for the same q1 as its second unclear attempt. Expect backend fallback containing verified explanation and reviewed linked primary follow-up; no diagnosis.
Moving to another question resets unclear attempt counter.
A supported diagnosis ends that question's clarification loop.

cases.student_explanation: They observed water and made a conclusion. Any conclusion from an observation is induction.
A prediction about the room is an explanation, so it has to be abduction.
cases.what_reviewers_should_assess: Distinguish prediction from explaining observed evidence.

cases.student_explanation: The rule talks about a whole club, so it must have been formed by induction. Applying it to Bea is induction too.
cases.what_reviewers_should_assess: Classify the presented inference, not an imagined origin of its premise.

cases.student_explanation: The jam warning and folded sheet prove the cause with absolute certainty, so this is deduction.
cases.what_reviewers_should_assess: Address claimed certainty; do not assert the printer has been repaired.

cases.student_explanation: Twelve successes turn the pattern into a rule that guarantees tomorrow's arrival.
Drawer B is just the best guess even though the question says those are the only two places and A is ruled out.

cases.what_reviewers_should_assess: Ask for reasoning; invent no misconception.
Ask which part supports the chosen category.

cases.student_explanation: I'm not sure how to explain it.
cases.what_reviewers_should_assess: Seek detail without attributing a belief.
Ask which feature of the inference matters.

cases.student_explanation: Maybe that one? I don't know.
Deduction always moves from a general rule to one specific case. This has two locations instead, so it cannot be deduction.
cases.what_reviewers_should_assess: Address the overly narrow definition of deduction.

cases.student_explanation: The person is acting like a detective. Detective work is always deductive, so choosing the likely cause must be deduction.
cases.what_reviewers_should_assess: Address occupation-based classification; avoid unrelated claims.
No inference about the learner's conceptual beliefs.

cases.student_explanation: I meant that Bea must have the badge if both statements are true, but I may have clicked the wrong label.
cases.what_reviewers_should_assess: Clarify the selection mismatch; do not invent a conceptual error.
